2: A bypass with no end date is a permanent hole in the filter.
QUIC isn't forwarded end to end, so a browser could carry web traffic around the service.
And a TLS inspection certificate authority that's compromised could impersonate any site to every managed device.

So the goal: show that the ring's web traffic is filtered by an identity-aware policy, that every exception has an owner and an end date, that QUIC can't slip past it, and that inspection runs from a dedicated authority, within an approved privacy scope, breaking under one percent of sessions.
